references.text: Continues the legislation concerning the treatment of slaves, specifically regarding release when there is physical injury to an eye or a tooth
The principle that whoever strikes a person and causes death must die - the foundational law on murder
Laws concerning slaves and their status in Israel, providing context for slave legislation
Laws about killing with weapons and the consequences of beating someone to death
The law of retaliation establishing the principle of just punishment
The foundational law that whoever strikes a man and causes his death must die - the same context for capital punishment
Numbers 35:20 defines the criteria for intentional murder (hatred), determining whether 'vengeance' in 21:20 is required.
Numbers 35:16 gives concrete criteria (an iron tool) to distinguish between murder and negligence, which is crucial for interpreting 21:20.
Numbers 35:18 expands the definition of deadly weapons, helping to assess the intent behind using a rod in 21:20.
Numbers 35:21 confirms that direct violence with premeditation constitutes murder regardless of the victim's status, supporting the requirement for vengeance in 21:20.
